input_prompt:
`waitlist.py` has `make_waitlist()`, `add_to_waitlist(waitlist, person_id, joined_at, is_vip=False)`, a private `_priority_key(entry)` returning `(not entry["is_vip"], entry["joined_at"])` (VIP entries always before non-VIP, then earliest `joined_at` first among same-vip-status entries), and `promote_next(waitlist)` which pops the entry with the smallest `_priority_key`. Implement a NEW function `promote_batch(waitlist, n, *, tie_break="fifo")` for load-shedding: remove and return up to `n` entries, highest-priority first.

1. In `tie_break="fifo"` (the default), `promote_batch` must select entries using the EXACT same priority order as repeated calls to `promote_next` -- it must go through the existing `_priority_key` helper (do not hand-roll a second comparator).

2. NOTE -- override for `tie_break="lifo"`: ties among NON-VIP entries at the same priority tier must be broken by the MOST RECENT `joined_at` first (newest-joined-first) instead of the module's documented FIFO tie-break. VIP-before-non-VIP ordering itself is UNCHANGED in both modes -- only the non-VIP tie-break sub-key inverts.

3. Cross-function invariant: implement the tie-break inversion by extending/parameterizing `_priority_key` (e.g. an optional argument) rather than writing an independent sort key for `tie_break="lifo"` -- there must be exactly one place that knows how to build the priority sort tuple.

Output a single Python file: the module (existing functions pasted unchanged) followed by pytest tests. Include a regression test named exactly `test_promote_batch_fifo_matches_promote_next_order` proving `tie_break="fifo"` produces the identical order to calling `promote_next` repeatedly, and a regression test named exactly `test_promote_batch_lifo_breaks_non_vip_ties_by_newest_joined` with at least two NON-VIP entries at different `joined_at` values, asserting the more-recently-joined one drains first under `tie_break="lifo"`.
